corpusSummary: Across 2026 social-science studies, the corpus reveals a growing focus on how large language models reshape trust, learning, health, and governance, while foregrounding methodological, ethical, and equity challenges. Evidence spans AI as a research tool, human-AI interaction and embodiment, AI-driven education and health messaging, and AI-enabled policy deliberation. Collectively, findings stress validation, transparency, responsible design, and context-aware use to avoid anthropomorphism, bias, and misuse.

themes.name: Trust, embodiment, and human–AI interaction dynamics
themes.description: Investigates how AI embodiment, perceived humanness, trust, and interaction styles shape user experiences, welfare, and decision-making across health, education, and workplace contexts.

themes.name: AI as a methodological instrument and governance in social science
themes.description: Synthesizes opportunities and limits of using LLMs for data analysis, coding, surveys, simulations, and governance, emphasizing validation, transparency, and ethical oversight.

themes.name: AI in education and learning: literacy, tutoring, and assessment
themes.description: Documents the role of GenAI in learning, tutoring, scaffolding, curriculum mapping, and assessment practices, while highlighting risks like overreliance and equity concerns.

themes.name: AI in health, misinformation, and health equity
themes.description: Covers AI-generated health information, misinformation mitigation, patient education, clinician support, and equity-focused governance in digital health.
